the New Economy requires a reform of the VAT system and that the New Economy will increase international tax competition.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues.
the question of whether the traditional tax systems of turnover taxation and income taxation can be maintained in the light of the New Economy.
the question whether the New Economy is able to cope with the tax system of the Old Economy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
electronic commerce is not the panacea for the tax problems of the New Economy, but rather the source of new challenges.
the current tax systems in the European Community are not capable of coping with the challenges posed by the New Economy, and that the current international tax system is in urgent need of reform.
the New Economy is not the end of the world for the state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tax systems of industrialized countries are not well equipped to deal with the New Economy.
the New Economy will be an additional challenge to the fiscal state.

the New Economy is likely to increase the pressure to tax international trade in digital goods and services and to tax international income flows, while it reduces the pressure for a harmonization of turnover taxes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the New Economy will not lead to a fundamental change of the current tax system.
the current tax systems in most OECD countries are not able to deal with the new challenges posed by the New Economy.
a reform of the tax system is inevitable in the light of the New Economy.
